# Literature Review {#sec-litreview}

LexiMin

P_init:
- Non-empty portfolio of panels that initiates the optimisation process. As there could be exponentially many panels, it just starts with a single arbitrary panel, then iteratively produces more through column generation.

C_aux:

- Property 1: The total probability assigned to all possible panels must sum to 1 (100%).

- Property 2: The selection probability of a person is the sum of all valid panels that include them.

- Property 3: For all unfixed (unselected) people, the selection probability must be at least a defined floor (minimum selection probability).

- Property 4: For all fixed (previously selected) people, the probability will be held constant.


Overall function:
LexiMin aims to maximise the minimum selection probability (floor) across all participants, which represents the minimum selection probability for the currently least-likely-to-be-chosen individuals.
It uses Lambda panel-weighting to list likelihood of every given panel iteration.
It creates a "fixed set" of participants whose probabilities were already locked in during previous iterative rounds.
It uses rho to maintain "fixed values" for selection likelihoods of members of the "fixed set".
And then lumps all feasible panel sets back into the Portfolio.
